text: Leo felt sick, so he stayed in bed with his phone. He wondered if he could still send a letter to his aunt in Spain that day. First he typed two words: post office. The assistant understood he wanted the nearest post office and told him it was ten minutes away and closed at five. Then Leo typed three words: stamp price Spain. The assistant said a letter to Spain cost about two euros. Leo wrote back: bank open? The assistant checked and said the bank near the post office closed at four thirty. Leo sighed. He asked his big sister to go for him, and the assistant set a reminder for her to leave at three. Leo put the phone down and fell asleep.

Booking a haircut or a dentist visit means picking a day and a time the shop has free. The booking is there so you and the shop both know when you will arrive. People often change a booking. They move it to another day, make it earlier, or cancel it. They say things like, can you push my haircut to Friday, or I can't come on Monday, please cancel. Opening hours matter too, because it is true that no shop can take you when it is closed. So people ask, when do you open on Saturday? If you come by car, ask where to park. Some waiting rooms even have a small purifier to keep the air fresh while you wait.

Omar drove a delivery van all day, and by evening his ears were tired of engine noise. He sat down by the dryer, waiting for his socks, and spoke to the smart speaker on the shelf. Search for something funny to listen to, but not the news and not music, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted a comedy show with talking only. It found a short funny podcast about a cat that ran a shop, and it started playing it. After a minute Omar said, not so loud, please. The speaker turned the volume down from seven to four. Omar laughed at the cat joke and listened until the dryer buzzed.

Headlines are the short lines at the top of news stories. They tell you in a few words what happened, so you can decide what to read. A news app or a smart speaker can read them out each morning. People change the topic a lot. They say, give me sports instead, or only local news please, or fewer stories today. Local news might tell you that a truck broke down on the main road, or that a new bakery is selling a delicious pie. Some people like calm news, so they ask for good news only and chill with a cup of tea. You can stop the headlines at any time by saying, that's enough.

Person: Hello, can you get a room for me and my mom?
Assistant: Yes, I can help. Which night do you want to stay?
Person: We get there tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Good. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Two nights. Mom says the room must be warm. Can you heat it before we come?
Assistant: I can't control the heat in the room, but I can ask the hotel to turn it on. Is that okay?
Person: Yes please. And does it have a network for the tablet?
Assistant: Yes, the hotel has a free wifi network. Breakfast is healthy and starts at eight.
Person: Great, thank you!

Rosa came home after a night shift at the hospital. She was tired, but she wanted to work on a hand painted invitation for her sister's party. She said to her phone, find me a good painting class this Tuesday. The assistant found a class at six in the evening. Rosa thought about it and said, no wait, Wednesday, I work Tuesday. The assistant understood she wanted to change the day, so it looked again and found a Wednesday class at the same time. Then Rosa asked it to reduce the brightness of her screen so it would not hurt her eyes. The assistant did that and saved the class in her calendar. Rosa smiled and went to bed.

name: spell_word
does: Shows the correct spelling of a single word and says it out loud, one letter at a time.
inputs: the word, and the language if it is not English
people say:
- How do I write hat in Spanish?
- Is it p-a-i-n-t or p-a-n-t?
- Spell that last word for me, slowly.
- I always get this one wrong, can you check it?
- What letters are in the French word for apple?

Nina was late. She grabbed a plate of toast, and zoomed around the kitchen looking for her keys. The train station was twenty-five minutes away, and she was going to meet a friend from Paris. At the open door she shouted to her phone, how do I say where is the train station in French? The assistant understood she needed a short phrase to say out loud. It answered with the French words and said them slowly so she could hear them. Nina repeated them twice. Then she said, save that for later, and the assistant put the phrase in her notes. Nina ate her toast on the walk and ran for the train.

Sam drove a bus in the early shift, and he got home in the afternoon with a bad headache. The sun came right through the living room window. His mother was resting in the next room, so he did not want to shout. He grabbed his phone and typed in a hurry: close the blnds a bit. The assistant understood that he meant the blinds in the living room and that he wanted them only partly closed. It lowered them about halfway and told him so. Sam felt better. When his mother answered a call from his aunt in the other room, he asked the assistant to open the blinds in her room for fresh air. It did that too.

Maria was a cook, and she had a long day at the restaurant ahead. In the morning she told the smart garden helper, run the sprinklers for ten minutes. The assistant said okay and got ready to start. Then Maria looked at the grass. It was October, and the lawn was not very dry. No wait, make it five minutes, she said. The assistant understood that she had changed her mind, so it set the time to five minutes and said it would only water the inside part of the lawn, near the house. Maria welcomed the shorter time. She also asked it to stop the sprinklers when it started to rain, and the assistant said it would.

Person: I want to put my pancake breakfast on the calendar.
Assistant: Sure. What day and what time?
Person: Oh, I don't know how you say it. Tomorrow at nine, I think.
Assistant: Tomorrow at nine in the morning. Who is coming?
Person: Just my neighbor. Is it true you can send her a note?
Assistant: I can't send notes, but I can set a reminder for you to call her. Would that help?
Person: Yes, that is good. And a reminder to slice the fruit.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at eight to slice the fruit.

Mina had just moved to the city, and her phone battery was always low. One evening she said, my battery is almost dead and I'm far from home, where is a charging spot near me? The assistant understood she needed a place to charge. It found a cafe two streets away and told her the way. Then Mina said, also turn on do not disturb tomorrow at seven, because she wanted a quiet morning. The assistant set it for seven in the morning. She was carrying her guitar, so she could not type. She asked the assistant to dim the screen, and it did. At the cafe she fed her phone to the charger and ordered a tea.

Tom was a gardener, and he wore grey gloves all day. In his lunch break he sat on a bench and spoke to his phone. Show me only the unread emails, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to skip the old ones, so it listed just five unread emails. One of them said a package was on its way. Tom said, read that one, and the assistant read it out loud. Then he said, tell Dana the package will come half an hour later, and the assistant wrote a short email to Dana and asked, shall I send it? Tom said yes. The assistant sent the email, and Tom went back to his roses.

Person: I need to order an iron.
Assistant: Okay. Do you want a small travel iron or a big one for home?
Person: A travel one. I sleep in my truck a few nights a week and my shirts get wrinkled.
Assistant: Good idea. Where should I send it?
Person: I don't have a house address. Can you send it to my work?
Assistant: I can send it to a delivery locker or a shop near your work. Which one do you want?
Person: The locker is better. It has to come in twenty-five days at most, or I will finish my trip first.
Assistant: Delivery will take five days, so it will be early. I will order it now.

A water bill tells you how much water your home used and how much money you must pay. It comes once a month or every few months. The main body of the bill shows the amount, and the due date is near the top. People like to get their bills on time, so they stay calm and avoid late fees. When something changes, they use simple words. They say, move my due date to the first of the month, or send the bill by email instead of by post, or pay it every month by itself. If the amount looks too high, they say, why is it more than last time? A helper can find the answer or check the number for you.

Person: whats the watr temperature at the beach?
Assistant: I can look that up. Which beach do you mean?
Person: the big one near the pier, im new here
Assistant: Near the pier the water is about sixty-eight degrees today. It is a little cold.
Person: ok. is there a party there tonight?
Assistant: I don't know about parties. I can only tell you about the sun, the tides and the water.
Person: no problem. will i get cooked by the sun at noon?
Assistant: The sun is strong at noon today, so wear sun cream. Do you want a reminder to put it on?
Person: yes, and remind me to charge my phone

Going to the post office is a common errand. You walk through the door, take a number, and wait in line. It is for sending letters, picking up parcels and paying small bills. Waiting can hurt your feet, so many people ask for the quiet times. They say, when is it least busy? Others ask, is the post office open on Saturday? If you have an old parcel waiting for you, you might say, remind me to pick up my parcel on Friday. Some people want a different place, so they ask, where is the nearest pickup point? Then the helper finds a place and gives you the hours and the way.

name: ink_deal_helper
does: Looks for a discount on ink and paper that fit the user's printer and tells where to buy them.
inputs: the printer model, and what the person wants to buy
people say:
- My printer is out of black ink, and I'm in a hurry, what's the cheapest place?
- Is there a sale on paper this week?
- Find me a coupon for color cartridges.
- Write a polite note to the shop asking if they can match a lower price.
- I need ink for my old printer today, nothing too fancy.

A navigation app tells you how to get from one place to another and how long it will take. At night the app often shows quieter roads and fewer cars, so a trip may be faster. People can change the route as they drive. They say, avoid the highway, take the shortest way, or find a way with no tolls. They also ask, how long will it take if I leave at eight? Some drivers want to stay on big, well lit roads after dark. They say, use main roads only. When a driver gets hungry, they might say, find a tasty place to eat on the way. The app then changes the route and adds a short stop.

Traffic on a map is shown with colors. Green means the road is open, and purple or dark red means cars are moving very slowly. The map is there to help you pick the best road before you leave. When weather is bad, like heavy rain or lightning, roads get slow, and the map updates to show it. People who love a smooth trip ask for changes. They say, show me another way, or is there a faster road right now? If they are late, they say, how long until I get there? And if they want to leave early to miss the rush, they say, tell me the best time to go.

When you book a hotel room, you choose the day you arrive, the number of nights and the number of guests. The hotel keeps the room for you. Check-in is the time when you can get your key, and check-out is when you must leave. People often change a booking. They say, make it three nights instead of two, or add one more guest, or can we check in earlier? Some people want a room with a nice view, so they ask for a room that looks outside at the garden. Others ask about breakfast, and whether it has fresh bread and carrots in the salad. Guests who run in the morning can ask where the park is.

Ben woke up slowly, with blurry eyes. His phone was on the cold floor next to the bed, and he picked it up with a sleepy hand. The words on the screen looked too tiny to read, and a message from his boss said something about the notice board at work. Ben said, I can't see anything on this thing. The assistant understood that he did not mean the phone was broken, but that the text was too small. It made the letters bigger and asked, is this better? Ben said yes. Then the screen started to freeze for a second, so Ben asked the assistant to read the message to him out loud, and it did.

A step counter is a small tool in your phone or on your wrist. It counts every step you take and shows how far you have walked. People use it to make a daily goal, like eight thousand steps. They change things all the time. They say, set my goal to ten thousand, or show me how far I ran this week, or what was my pace today? If they stop the counter by mistake, they say, undo that. Many walkers like a quiet park or a calm road, so they also say, find me a quiet route for a short walk. The helper then picks a way and tells them the distance.

They want to know the Spanish word for grilled chicken.
What's chicken in Spanish?
Say grilled chicken in Spanish, please.
How would a waiter in Madrid call grilled chicken?
I need the exact word for it on a menu.
Tell me the Spanish for grilled chicken, and say it at half speed.
I have twenty-five seconds before I order, what do I say?
Could you please tell me the word, because I do not want to point at the picture again?
Spanish for grilled chicken, thanks.

Kofi had just moved to the city, and he wanted to find a team to cheer for. One cloudy Saturday, he made a cup of tea and asked his phone, who plays today? The assistant understood he wanted the matches in town. It told him two teams played at three, and a smaller game started at six. Kofi asked, which one has more fans? The assistant said the three o'clock game was twice as big. He said, okay, tell me when it starts, so the assistant set a reminder for half past two. Later he asked for the score. The assistant said it was one to zero, and Kofi cheered loudly in his kitchen.

An alarm wakes you up at a time you choose. A timer counts down from a time you pick, like ten minutes for pasta. People use alarms often, and sometimes more than one, because they can sleep through the first. They change them all the time. They say, wake me at six thirty instead of seven, or move my alarm one hour later, or turn off my Monday alarm. When a timer rings, people say, snooze for five minutes or add two more minutes. Some people say, set a timer so I don't pay the parking fee when my time runs out. Others set one before the beach, so they don't forget their sunglasses.

Priya owned a small shop, and a customer had asked her to deliver a box of tea across town. She was in a hurry, so she typed to her phone with one thumb: hwo long to drive to elm street. The assistant understood the typo and knew she meant the drive to Elm Street. It said the trip would take twenty minutes. Priya typed, skip the highway, there is a thin lane near it, and the assistant found a way with small roads that took twenty-five minutes. She did not like to climb stairs with heavy boxes, so she asked if there was parking near the building. The assistant found one two blocks away.

Jun was a student, and his friends were coming over for a small party in twenty minutes. The flat was too quiet and a bit sad. He said, it's so quiet in here. The assistant understood that he did not just describe the room, but that he wanted some music, so it played a happy playlist at a low volume. Jun saw dirty spots on the floor and had to mop quickly. He asked the assistant to set a ten minute timer, and he was patient with the old mop. Then the pizza man arrived, and Jun asked how to do the payment. The assistant opened the app, and Jun tapped to pay.

name: sun_glare_blinds
does: Tilts the blinds to the right angle so the sun does not shine in the eyes or fade the furniture.
inputs: which room, and how much light the person wants
people say:
- The sun is right in my eyes.
- My red sofa is losing its color, can you do something?
- I hope you can make the room less bright.
- Block the afternoon light in the kitchen.
- It's too sunny to watch my show.

name: watch_party_planner
does: Picks a show, sets a start time and sends an invite to friends so they can watch together.
inputs: the show, the time, and who to invite
people say:
- Let's watch the game with Ana and Luis tonight.
- Invite my cousins to see the new show at eight.
- Can you set up a movie night with friends? Popcorn bucket is ready.
- Tell everyone we start the series on Friday.
- I want my friends inside the same stream as me.

A lawn mower or a robot mower cuts the grass so that it stays short and tidy. In September the grass grows more slowly, so many people cut it less often. A robot mower can move around the garden by itself and go back to its base when it is done. People change how it works. They say, mow the lawn on Thursday instead of Wednesday, or cut the grass a little shorter, or skip today because it is wet. They also like smooth edges, so they say, trim the edge of the lawn along the path. If the mower gets stuck, they say, stop mowing and come home.

Chen was in a hurry to leave the house, but the rooms were cold. He said to the thermostat, set the heat to twenty-two degrees. Then he thought about the cost of heating a house. It was expensive in winter. No, make it twenty, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to fix the number, so it changed the temperature to twenty degrees. Chen also did not want the heat to run all day. He asked it to turn the heating off at eight, because he would be at work, and to pick it up again at five. The assistant set both times. Then Chen picked up his bag and went out.

They want the plants in the garden to get water.
Water the plants.
Give the flowers a drink.
Turn on the sprinklers for a bit.
Can you shift the watering to the evening?
The water in the can is stale, so please use fresh water from the tap for the tomatoes.
It hasn't rained all week, so would you please start the garden hose?
I have homework tonight and won't be home until late, so could you kindly water the plants for me at six?
My plants look thirsty.

name: cinema_time_finder
does: Finds the times a film is on at the cinemas near the person and says which ones still have seats.
inputs: the film or the kind of film, the day, and the town
people say:
- What's on tonight after the gym?
- When can I see that new space film?
- I'm ironing my shirt, tell me what time the comedy starts.
- Any extra shows late on Saturday?
- Where is the cheapest ticket for a family film?

name: pause_show_timer
does: Pauses the show for a set time and starts it again by itself when the time is up.
inputs: how long to wait
people say:
- Hold on, I'm thirsty and need a drink.
- Stop it for five minutes, someone is at the door.
- Wait, I have to answer the phone, pause until I come back.
- Don't miss the scene with the factory, pause for two minutes.
- Freeze the show and start it again at nine.

Lara was new in the city and in a new school. At night she wanted to check her work, so she typed in a hurry: whens my scince homework due. The assistant understood the typo and knew she meant science. It looked at her list and said the science homework was due on Thursday. Lara typed, what is it about? The assistant said it was about the water cycle and a short page about speed. She wanted to study in silence, so she said, turn on a silent timer for thirty minutes. The assistant started a timer with no sound and only a small light when it was done.

Person: It's freezing in this empty flat.
Assistant: I'm sorry it's cold. Do you want me to turn up the heat?
Person: Yes please. Daily I come here after my shift and it's always cold.
Assistant: Which room should I warm up? The living room or the bedroom?
Person: Bedroom. The dust from the boxes makes me sneeze, too.
Assistant: I can't clean the dust, but I can start the air filter if the room has one.
Person: It has. Do that, and put the heat to twenty. I will pack my last bottle of water now.
Assistant: Done. The bedroom will be warm in about ten minutes.

Dani was a teenager, and she typed to her phone while eating a slice of delicious cake. Dim the lights and tell me how many days until my birthday, she wrote. The assistant understood that there were two things. First it made the lights in her room softer. Then it counted the days and said her birthday was in twenty-two days. Dani smiled and wrote, ask the bakery what size the cake is for ten people. The assistant said it would send a message. Dani put her fork down, because she was already thinking about the party and the candles.

After a long night at the hospital, Hana sat down at her desk to draw. She loved to draw a storm with lightning and a bowl of juicy peaches on the table. She said to her tablet, select the thick pencil. The assistant chose the thick pencil tool. Hana thought for a moment and said, no, the thin pencil. The assistant understood that she had changed her mind, so it picked the thin pencil instead. Then she asked it to play soft rain sounds, and she started drawing. When her eyes got heavy, she told the assistant to save the picture and turn off the lamp.

Kai lay in bed, nervous about a call with his cousin in Tokyo. He had just come out of the shower and did not know if it was too late to call. He typed two words: Tokyo time? The assistant understood he wanted to know what time it was in Tokyo right now. It answered that it was seven in the morning there. Kai felt better, because his cousin would be awake. Then he typed, remind me, and the assistant asked, when? Kai said in ten minutes. The assistant set the reminder, and Kai picked up his phone to call.

name: quiet_night_mode
does: Makes the phone and speakers silent at bedtime, so no sound or light wakes the person.
inputs: the bedtime, and the time to wake up
people say:
- I want a silent night, please.
- Stop my speaker from talking after ten.
- Don't let any brand of app buzz me while I sleep.
- Go quiet until seven in the morning.
- It's my bedtime, switch everything to sleep.

The water heater in a house keeps water hot so you can take a warm shower or wash dishes. A leak is when water drips from a pipe or a wall. A small leak can use a lot of water, so people watch the water use. Sometimes a stain on the wall or a wet floor shows a leak. When the heater is upstairs, you may hear the water breathe in the pipes. People ask for changes. They say, make the water a bit cooler, or turn the water heater off while we are away, or how much water did we use this week? If they see a drip, they say, tell me if there is a leak.

Person: Can you change my ribbon to inches and tell me the weight of a flour bag in pounds?
Assistant: Yes. How long is the ribbon, and how heavy is the flour bag?
Person: The ribbon is two meters. It's for a party banner in my shop. The flour is five kilos.
Assistant: Two meters is about seventy-nine inches. Five kilos is about eleven pounds.
Person: Simple. Can you also call the party store and ask if they are in a rush this week?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make calls. I can give you the number of the store if you like.
Person: Yes please, that is fine.

Ines was a busy parent, and the kids were shouting in the next room. She had a paper from the bakery with a good price on a birthday cake, but she wanted a copy. Scan this page, she said to the printer helper, but don't print it. The assistant understood she wanted only a file, so it scanned the page and saved it on her phone. Then Ines said, email it to my husband, and not to the whole family. The assistant sent the file to her husband only. Ines said thanks, picked up the paper, and ran to see why the kids were still shouting.

Writing starts with a draft, which is a first try. You write your ideas down, and then you go back and fix them. Editing means changing words, checking spelling and making sentences shorter. Most writing programs show a word count, so you know how long your text is. People ask for changes in simple words. They say, make this shorter, or check my spelling, or change this word to something better. At night, when tired, it is easy to spot a mistake too late, so many people say, read it back to me. A good helper reads the text aloud, and you can hear if it sounds right.

Dee came home from a night shift at the clinic with cold feet. The kitchen was empty, and she opened the cupboard. I'm out of coffee, she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she did not say what to do, but that she wanted coffee on her shopping list, so it added coffee. Then she said, order a camping chair for the weekend. The assistant found a chair with free delivery and asked, shall I order it? Dee said yes and asked to mark the order as a gift for her brother. The assistant did it. Dee made a cup of tea and went to bed.

Tim was a child who loved to walk. One evening he asked the family speaker, how many steps did I take today and what is the way to the park? The speaker understood two questions. First it said he took six thousand steps. Then it told him the park was ten minutes away. Tim worried that he would not reach his goal of eight thousand. The speaker said he only needed two thousand more, and that the park trip would be enough. Tonight he felt proud. He asked the speaker to tell his dad, and the speaker left a note for him on the fridge screen.

Person: I don't want to be cold. Can you make it warm?
Assistant: Yes. Which room do you want to warm up?
Person: My room. But I don't want the radiator to get hot, it's too hot to touch.
Assistant: Okay. I will turn the heat up a little, not a lot. Would twenty-one degrees be fine?
Person: Yes. Mom said I can swim after school, so I will need a warm room when I come back.
Assistant: Good plan. When do you come back?
Person: At four. I will play on the grass until then.
Assistant: I will warm your room at half past three.

They want the room to be warmer, but just a little.
A bit warmer, please.
Turn the heat up by one degree.
It's rainy and my desk is cold, can you raise it?
Make it a little cozier in here.
Can we have half a degree more?
Cut the chill in the living room.
I'd like it two degrees warmer than now, and not more.
Would you kindly turn the heating up a bit, since my fingers are cold when I write?

Sofia owned a small shop, and tonight she was having a party for her customers. She was hungry, but there was a lot to do. She asked her phone, how many people said yes to the invitation? The assistant knew the guest list and said twenty-five people had said yes. Sofia said, then I need twenty-five peach tarts. The assistant did not know how to bake, but it found a bakery that could make them, and it put the order in her notes. She asked it to play lively music at six. The assistant said it would start the playlist then. Sofia ate a quick snack and hung the last lights.
